questions.q: Why does this lesson say a design that lives only in one architect's head has little practical value?
options: Because Salesforce requires all designs to be stored in a specific tool
Because nobody else can act on it correctly if they can't understand or evaluate it
Because unwritten designs are always technically wrong
Because a design must always be at least 20 pages long to count
questions.explain: Communication is the mechanism by which a design actually becomes real — a design nobody else understands can't be approved, funded, or built correctly, regardless of how technically sound it is.

questions.q: What is the specific difference between what a diagram does and what a narrative does?
options: A diagram explains why; a narrative shows structure
A diagram shows structure (the pieces and connections); a narrative explains the reasoning behind that structure
They do the exact same job, so only one is ever needed
A narrative is only used for security-related designs
questions.explain: A diagram shows what the pieces are and how they connect; a narrative explains why the structure is shaped that way and what trade-off it makes. Neither substitutes for the other.

questions.q: In the four-part decision-presentation structure, what should come first?
options: The alternative that was considered and rejected
The decision itself, stated in one sentence, before any justification
The decision's main known weakness
A list of every factor that was ever considered
questions.explain: Stating the decision first lets the audience know what's actually being proposed before they have to follow the reasoning behind it, so they can push back on something specific rather than vaguely.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what's the right response when a reviewer raises a challenge the architect hadn't fully considered?
options: Defend the original design regardless, to avoid looking unprepared
Immediately agree with everything the reviewer says without evaluating it
Restate the challenge to confirm understanding, then either explain the existing reasoning or genuinely acknowledge the gap and say what you'd do about it
End the review and reschedule it for another day
questions.explain: Treating a challenge as useful information rather than an attack means actually processing it — confirming you understood it, then either pointing to the real reasoning that already accounts for it, or honestly acknowledging a genuine gap.

questions.q: What does this lesson say a CTA review board panel is actually testing for when it challenges a candidate's design?
options: Whether the candidate's first design was already perfect
Whether the candidate can take a real challenge, process it, and respond with genuine reasoning instead of collapsing or stonewalling
Whether the candidate can speak for the longest amount of time
Whether the candidate agrees with every challenge automatically
questions.explain: The review board format is built around challenging a design and watching how the candidate responds — the test is the quality of that real-time reasoning under challenge, not whether the original design needed zero changes.
